Despite a gallant effort Morrison was forced back to third but in finishing only fourteen seconds behind Guildford & Godalming and six behind Mitcham we can consider our team to have performed admirably; especially when we were without Jack Hampshire.
Stan's victory was scored in the A.A.A Championships against an International class field. July J.
The most successful was Jack Hampshire who finished 7th in the Youth mile final with 4:32.3. He finished second in his heat with a time of 4:33.6.

David Cocks was in great form setting a track record for the Junior 880 with 1:59.3 - half a second faster than the Senior winner! Jack Hampshire (2:08.3) backed up well for 3rd place. The Junior mile was also a Belgrave party.

Jack Hampshire,as usual in the big races, really pulled his weight and was our third scorer in 61st position. Our Youths team packed in their usual order with Simmons (31) Edwards (41) and Leaver (103) being Bicourt's supporting string yet again.

In the Junior match Dave Wiseman cantered home in the quarter in 52.0 secs. and Jack Hampshire took the half in 2:7.6. Pottinger once again proved himself a mainstay in the field events by taking the long jump and the weight.
Alan Morrison, Dave Cocks, and Jack Hampshire have been other regular members of the junior team and have had good and indifferent runs alike.
Further down the field Jack Hampshire was making sure of fourth spot, and Joe MacDonald caused a certain amount of amusement by differing with the lap scorers on exactly how many laps he had left.
Within a mile the leading bunch of four - Bicourt,Cocks,Hampshire and Major - were well clear of the field,with Jack Hampshire making the pace.

It was good to see John Woodcock back again after a period of studying, and Jack Hampshire having a go once again. But the boquet of the day goes to the man who won gold, Lionel Mann, for it was only 4 days earlier that he had placed third in the Belgrave 20 miles road race with a Club record time of 1:44:45!
…nyones guess who would triumph in this Club championship, and with the prospect of holding for a year that much coveted Jack Hampshire trophy to spur them on, each was out to be the first man home.…

The defending champion Adrian Cook had no trouble and took the 'Jack Hampshire Trophy' once again. A Colts race was held in conjunction and who should pop up once again but Gary Budinger with a tremendous run that took him well clear of the next runner.
